images.caption: Front of the James E. Marshall House, located at 514 Wayne Street in Sandusky, Ohio, United States.  Built in 1875, it is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.

brief: An island-town cottage lot: James E. Marshall House, a 19th-century Lake Erie house; see the photo for its massing, porch and trim. One photo; year estimated. Older than 1970: the Lake Erie shore towns that stand in for Victory Bay's island streets (Vermilion, Sandusky, Put-in-Bay) were built 1840-1920, and Commons has almost no newer cottages there. Foundations taken deeper than needed (spec rule 4).

facade.notes: the James E. Marshall House (Sandusky OH): a white five-bay centre-gable house with an ornamented gable (bargeboard), bracketed cornice, fancy pedimented window hoods picked out in green, a bracketed door hood with a carved panel, a limestone base; a cast-iron fence along the sidewalk, two columnar evergreens

why.note: the five-bay centre-hall house, with a picturesque centre gable
a merchant's cast-iron fence on a port-city street
